  aPropertyKindCalculus.ScaleType =Eq.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} : α → α → PropThe equality relation. It has one introduction rule, `Eq.refl`.
We use `a = b` as notation for `Eq a b`.
A fundamental property of equality is that it is an equivalence relation.
```
variable (α : Type) (a b c d : α)
variable (hab : a = b) (hcb : c = b) (hcd : c = d)

example : a = d :=
  Eq.trans (Eq.trans hab (Eq.symm hcb)) hcd
```
Equality is much more than an equivalence relation, however. It has the important property that every assertion
respects the equivalence, in the sense that we can substitute equal expressions without changing the truth value.
That is, given `h1 : a = b` and `h2 : p a`, we can construct a proof for `p b` using substitution: `Eq.subst h1 h2`.
Example:
```
example (α : Type) (a b : α) (p : α → Prop)
        (h1 : a = b) (h2 : p a) : p b :=
  Eq.subst h1 h2

example (α : Type) (a b : α) (p : α → Prop)
    (h1 : a = b) (h2 : p a) : p b :=
  h1 ▸ h2
```
The triangle in the second presentation is a macro built on top of `Eq.subst` and `Eq.symm`, and you can enter it by typing `\t`.
For more information: [Equality](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/quantifiers_and_equality.html#equality)

At runtime, strings are represented by [dynamic arrays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_array)

Planned. Pulls in PhysLib + Mathlib as a separate library (the spine stays Mathlib-free). Each base SI kind is assigned its unit dimension; derived kinds get the product/quotient of their factors' dimensions.

The dimension map \dim : \mathrm{KindOfProperty} \to \mathrm{Dimension} sends a kind-of-property to its PhysLib Dimension (ℚ-exponents over length/mass/time/charge/temperature). It is deliberately many-to-one: that is what makes the dimension-1 disambiguation true.
Planned. A predicate Extensive k asserting additivity of measure over a Decomposition of the carrier system.

A kind is extensive when, for any partition of a system into disjoint parts, the quantity of the whole equals the sum over the parts. This requires the mereological structure deferred from the foundations chapter.
Planned. Defined from KMul by reassociating the triple, inheriting the same coherence side-condition.

\mathrm{KDiv}\ k_3\ k_2\ k_1 is the division dual of the kind product: k_3 divided by k_2 yields k_1. Fuel-consumption \times rainfall is the classic Flater example whose careless handling yields a category error rather than a number.
Planned. A relation (or a structure of asserted product-edges) over kinds, with each edge required to satisfy \dim k_3 = \dim k_1 \cdot \dim k_2.

\mathrm{KMul}\ k_1\ k_2\ k_3 holds when kind k_1 times kind k_2 yields kind k_3. It is partial and curated: an application asserts the legitimate products of its kinds, each carrying the dimensional coherence obligation discharged by the homomorphism theorem.
A structure with DecidableEq. IsQuantity, and the scale divisions IsNominal/IsOrdinal/IsDifferential/IsRational (§13.2), are definitional predicates over the scale field.

A kind-of-property (§6.19) bundles a terminological id, a scale (from the scale types), and an optional examination principle. A kind is a kind-of-quantity (§13.3.1) iff its scale has magnitude (is at least ordinal).
An existential over a shared upper bound.

Two kinds are mutually comparable iff they share a common super-kind (\exists p,\ a \sqsubseteq p \wedge b \sqsubseteq p). This is how width and height stay comparable as lengths while remaining distinct sub-kinds. Uses specialization.
Planned. A structure Quantity (k : KindOfProperty) carrying a numeric magnitude, with arithmetic gated by k.scale (per the proved operator stratification, operator monotonicity).

A quantity Quantity k is a magnitude of a fixed kind k. It is indexed by k, a kind-of-property, so the type system forbids forming or comparing a Quantity k₁ with a Quantity k₂ when k_1 \neq k_2 — even if both kinds are dimension one. This indexing is the fix for the dimension-1 conflation.
A four-constructor inductive with a rank : ScaleType → Nat and the induced ≤. The lemmas le_def, le_refl, le_trans, and le_antisymm establish that ≤ is the expected linear order.

The four scale types of Dybkær Fig. 12.21, ordered by operator richness: \mathrm{nominal} \sqsubset \mathrm{ordinal} \sqsubset \mathrm{interval} \sqsubset \mathrm{ratio}, admitting respectively \{=,\neq\}, then \{<,>\}, then \{+,-\}, then \{\times,\div\}.
An inductive with refl and step constructors; of_edge lifts a single edge.

Specialization Specializes E is the reflexive–transitive closure of a direct-parent edge relation E over kind-of-property. Different E give different per-application hierarchies — the extensibility a fixed inductive would deny.
A one-field structure with DecidableEq; nothing to prove. The synonym Object := System keeps the instance layer reading as "characterizes an object".

A system (Dybkær §3.3) is a demarcated arrangement of elements and their relationships; object (§3.3 Note 6) is given as a synonym. Modelled abstractly by identity here; the mereological structure that extensivity needs is added in a later module.
Planned. A Unit k := { ref : Quantity k } (or a chosen nonzero reference), with measure : Quantity k → Unit k → ℝ giving the numeric value in that unit.

A unit Unit k is a distinguished quantity of kind k chosen as the reference: measuring expresses any quantity of kind k as \text{number} \times \text{unit}. Because Unit is indexed by the same k, "a metre" and "a unit of gravimetric water content" inhabit different types.
Reflexivity takes the witness a itself; symmetry swaps the two halves of the conjunction.
Mutual comparability is reflexive (refl) and symmetric (symm), and any specialization induces it (of_specializes). Uses mutual comparability.

Planned. By the construction of KMul: a well-formed kind product is defined by composing the factors, and dim is defined to distribute over that composition, so the equation holds by rfl/unfolding plus Dimension's commutative-group laws from PhysLib.

Dimensional coherence — \dim is a homomorphism. Whenever the interaction algebra says k_1 and k_2 combine to k_3, their dimensions combine the same way: \mathrm{KMul}\ k_1\ k_2\ k_3 \;\Longrightarrow\; \dim k_3 = \dim k_1 \cdot \dim k_2. This is the theorem that licenses forgetting to the dimension layer without losing soundness: a kind-level product is always dimensionally consistent. Builds on the dimension map and the kind product.

Planned. vwc and gwc are declared as distinct KindOfProperty values (distinct id, distinct examination principle), so vwc ≠ gwc is by decide. Both have dim = 1 once the dimension map is in place, giving a witnessed \exists k_1\ k_2,\ k_1 \neq k_2 \wedge \dim k_1 = \dim k_2.

The dimension-1 disambiguation (the motivating capstone). There exist distinct kinds that map to the same dimension. Concretely, for volumetric and gravimetric water content, \mathrm{vwc} \neq \mathrm{gwc} \qquad\text{yet}\qquad \dim(\mathrm{vwc}) = \dim(\mathrm{gwc}) = \mathbf{1}, and likewise for permittivity, reflectivity, and emissivity. So the kind layer is a strict refinement of the dimension layer: \dim is not injective. This is the statement PhysLib — and any dimension-only model, whether OWL2 or a representation-rooted hierarchy like SysML v2's — structurally cannot make. Uses kind-of-property and the dimension map.
Planned. By induction on the decomposition, using the additivity field of Extensive k at each split.

Extensive aggregation. For an extensive kind k and a system decomposed into parts s_1, \dots, s_n, \mathrm{value}_k\Bigl(\bigsqcup_i s_i\Bigr) = \sum_i \mathrm{value}_k(s_i). The \forall-quantified additivity law itself — not a single instance — is the deliverable, and it is exactly what OWL2 has no vocabulary for. Builds on extensive kinds.
Planned. Immediate from defining KDiv as the reassociation of KMul; the round-trip is the symmetry of that definition.

Multiplication and division are inverse on kinds. Whenever a product is defined, dividing the result by one factor recovers the other: \mathrm{KMul}\ k_1\ k_2\ k_3 \;\Longrightarrow\; \mathrm{KDiv}\ k_3\ k_2\ k_1. Together with dimensional coherence this is the calculus that OWL2 cannot host: an algebraic law with arithmetic side-conditions, proved rather than consistency-checked. Builds on the kind product and the kind quotient.
Planned. A concrete two-part decomposition with measured volumes whose mixture volume is smaller, witnessing \neg\,\mathrm{Extensive}\ \mathrm{volume} for that system.

Counterexample — volume on mixing is not extensive. Volume fails the additivity law for a water/ethanol mixture: the volume of the mixture is strictly less than the sum of the component volumes. Stating the negation keeps the extensive predicate honest. Uses extensive kinds.
Unfold IsQuantity, IsNominal, and HasMagnitude; the scale is nominal, so scale ≠ nominal is false.
A nominal kind is, by construction, not a kind-of-quantity: it has no magnitude. Uses kind-of-property.
Decide all sixteen ordered pairs: cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [AllowsOrder, AllowsDifference, AllowsRatio, le_def, rank].

Operator-availability monotonicity. A richer scale licenses every operation a poorer one does: if a \le b then AllowsOrder, AllowsDifference, and AllowsRatio each transport from a to b. This is a meta-theorem OWL2's reasoner cannot even phrase, since it quantifies over which operations are defined for a kind. Builds on the scale types.
The scale is ratio, so scale ≠ nominal holds; unfold and simplify.
A rational kind is a kind-of-quantity. Uses kind-of-property.
Reflexivity and transitivity are inherited from Nat.le on rank. Antisymmetry reduces to Nat.le_antisymm on the ranks followed by a four-by-four case split (cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all).
The scale order is a linear order: reflexive (le_refl), transitive (le_trans), and antisymmetric (le_antisymm) on the scale types.
Transitivity is by induction on the first derivation: refl returns the second derivation, step re-applies the constructor under the inductive hypothesis.

Specialization is a preorder. It is reflexive (the refl constructor) and transitive (Specializes.trans). Stating — let alone proving — an algebraic law of the taxonomy is exactly what an OWL2 reasoner cannot do; it checks consistency, not laws. Uses specialization.
Planned. torque, angle, energy declared as kinds (angle dimension one); the product edge is asserted and its coherence checked; energy ≠ torque is by decide.

Worked instance. Torque times plane angle is energy, and energy is not torque, even though \dim(\mathrm{torque}) = \dim(\mathrm{energy}). Formally \mathrm{KMul}\ \mathrm{torque}\ \mathrm{angle}\ \mathrm{energy} holds while \mathrm{energy} \neq \mathrm{torque} — the small example that shows the algebra carrying information dimension alone discards. Uses the kind product.

Planned. The conversion factor is r = \mathrm{measure}(u_1, u_2) and its inverse r^{-1}; the round-trip is r^{-1}\cdot(r \cdot q) = q, requiring r \neq 0 from the chosen-reference nonzeroness. Ratio formation is licensed by the ratio scale.

Unit conversion is a faithful round-trip. For two units u_1, u_2 of the same kind k, converting a quantity from u_1 to u_2 and back is the identity: \mathrm{convert}_{u_2 \to u_1}\bigl(\mathrm{convert}_{u_1 \to u_2}(q)\bigr) = q. Conversion is multiplication by the ratio u_1 / u_2, defined only within a kind. There is no conversion between units of different kinds — that is a type error, not a runtime check. Builds on the unit definition.
